concepts.description: A recording artist or band, known by its name.

bindings.note: The album a track is on (the column allows none; every track in this data has one).

concepts.description: An album by one artist, known by its title.

bindings.note: The track bought on an invoice line.

concepts.description: One audio or video track that the store sells, usually on an album.
How long a track plays.
The price of one copy of a track in the catalogue (0.99 or 1.99). The price actually charged is on the invoice line (see unit-price).
A music genre such as Rock or Jazz, assigned to tracks.
The file format of a track, such as "MPEG audio file" or "Protected AAC audio file".

bindings.note: Playlist membership, one row per track on a playlist.

concepts.description: A named list of tracks. A track can be on many playlists and a playlist holds many tracks; PlaylistTrack records which track is on which list.

bindings.note: The customer who made a purchase.

concepts.description: A person who buys music from the store. Some customers name a company.
The country in the customer's address, as Chinook spells it ("USA", "Czech Republic"). For questions about where music is bought, use billing-country instead.
A member of the store's staff. Employee.Title is the job title.
The employee someone reports to. Empty for the general manager.
The employee who looks after a customer.

bindings.note: The invoice a line is on.

concepts.description: A billing invoice for tracks purchased by a customer. Chinook has 412 invoices dated from 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-22. It is an invoice record, not the request to supply represented by an order.
The date of a purchase. The time part is always midnight.

The country an invoice is billed to, as Chinook spells it ("USA", "Czech Republic"). Use this one when a question asks which countries buy or spend: it is recorded on the sale itself, and it is the column the saved per-capita query groups by. In this data it equals the customer's country on every invoice, but it would stay right if a customer moved. Chinook's spellings are matched to countries by the labels and aliases of the universal country concept ("USA" is an alias of United States).
One track bought on an invoice.
The amount charged on an invoice. It equals the sum of UnitPrice x Quantity over the invoice's lines (true for all 412 invoices).
The price charged for one copy of a track on an invoice line.
Copies of a track bought on one invoice line (always 1 in Chinook).
Money the store took for music. The data names no currency; Chinook's prices (0.99 and 1.99) are read as US dollars.

measure.formula: The sum of Invoice.Total over the invoices in scope. Summing InvoiceLine.UnitPrice x InvoiceLine.Quantity over the same invoices' lines gives the same amount.

concepts.description: Not in Chinook. The population of each billing country, from the World Bank, matched to Chinook's country names through the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the universal country concept. A country without a population figure drops out of per-capita results.

measure.formula: The World Bank's latest total population of the country.

concepts.description: Music sales in a country divided by its population, per million people, so that small and large countries can be compared. Answers "Which countries buy the most music relative to their population?".

measure.formula: For each billing country: music sales divided by the country's population, multiplied by 1,000,000. The order is highest first.

en: buy the most music relative to population

document.description: What the Chinook sample database means: a digital music store that sells tracks to customers in 24 countries. Each concept says what it is, the words people use for it, and which ModelSpec record type or field holds it, in which role. Concepts that are not specific to Chinook (country, currency, customer, invoice, price, revenue, date, population, per capita) are reused from the universal concepts at meaning://github.com/meaninggraph/core, each reference pinned to one commit with ?ref=.
document.name: Chinook music store

sources.note: Not part of Chinook. The latest observation per country. As of github.com/datatug/chinook-demo commit d2fc437 (data/geo/population_wb), the snapshot the DataTug Chinook demo uses, it is 2025 for all 24 Chinook countries.
sources.title: Population, total (World Development Indicators)
